target: native plant cell (PO_0025606) part of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), distal region
reason: Moss floras: the distal laminal cells of the leaf. A cell of a qualified whole (the leaf), in the distal region. No new class needed; the PO cell and leaf classes, with the region, express it.

target: native plant cell (PO_0025606) part of spore capsule operculum (PO_0030044)
reason: The cells of the moss capsule lid, often in rows twisted round the lid. A part of an existing PO class.

label: pseudoparaphyllium
parent: is_a PO_0005679 (plant epidermis); part_of PO_0030020 (gametophore axis)
definition: A portion of plant epidermis (PO:0005679) that is a foliose or filamentous outgrowth of a gametophore axis (PO:0030020), borne only around a branch primordium. NOTE: Differs from paraphyllium (PO:0030069), which is borne among the leaves along the axis.
reason: A real moss structure used in keys to pleurocarpous mosses in several floras. It is distinct from paraphyllium (position round branch primordia only), so it is not a synonym. Propose to PO upstream (Bryophytes subset), as a sibling of paraphyllium.

target: native plant cell (PO_0025606) part of leaf base (PO_0020040; synonym phyllid base)
reason: Moss leaves with a sheathing base: the cells of the lamina of the clasping base. A cell part of an existing leaf region. Narrower than leaf base.
'Perigonia as terminal discoid splash platforms': describes the form and function of the moss perigonium, not a separate part. Read as perigonium + discoid.

target: guard cell (PO_0000293); the wall is plant-type cell wall (GO:0009505) part of guard cell
reason: 'Inner walls thickened' of the stoma: the wall of the guard cells. PO has no cell wall class; GO:0009505 part of guard cell expresses it. If the patterns accept only PO/FLOPO bearers, fall back to guard cell.

target: native plant cell (PO_0025606) part of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075), distal region
reason: In these moss floras, 'upper cells' are the upper laminal cells of the leaf, the same as 'leaf distal cell'. The word alone does not say which organ, so it must only be read in a leaf context.

target: stereid (PO_0030045) part of costa (PO_0030072), adaxial side
reason: A band of stereids on the adaxial side of the moss leaf costa. Expressed as presence of stereid in the costa, with the side as position. No new class needed.
Moss leaf: the lamina at the leaf base; leaf base has the synonym phyllid base. Narrower: it is the lamina part of the base. 'Quadrate' here is said of its cells.
The quality 'enlarged' joined to the generic 'cell'. Like 'cell' in the previous review, it needs the organ it belongs to (here often the alar cells of the leaf base).

A real but narrow structure (a group of clear cells in the leaf axil of a few moss genera). Three statements do not justify a new class, and no existing class fits closely. Look at it again if more floras use it.

The cavity of a leaf cell. PO has no class for it, and moving the quality onto the cell would change the meaning (a quadrate cell can have a rounded lumen). 'lumen' was rejected in the previous review.

target: cortex (PO_0005708) part of gametophore axis (PO_0030020) or stem cortex (PO_0025612); count of cell layers
reason: A count of the cell layers in the stem cortex. The bearer is the cortex and the count is its number of layers (pattern 03). Not a new part.
The beak of the moss capsule lid is its drawn-out apex. Expressed as the apex of an existing class. 'beak' alone was rejected as generic; this compound names its organ.
'Specialized asexual reproduction [structures] absent': a generic phrase for gemmae, brood bodies and other propagules. No single class.
Narrower: a goitre-like swelling on one side of the moss capsule neck, the base of the sporangium (synonyms apophysis, hypophysis). The swelling can be read as sporangium base + swollen.

target: native plant cell (PO_0025606) part of leaf base (PO_0020040), just above the alar cells (PO_0030057)
reason: The leaf cells just above the alar region of a moss leaf. They are cells of the leaf base, not alar cells, so not a synonym of PO_0030057.
A piece of a ratio ('acumina 0.6-1 times the basal leaf length'). Handled by pattern 10 (ratio to another part), not a part name.
A width fragment with the unit lost ('distal laminal cells 7--10 [µm] wide').
A quality (fused, connate) with a count, not a part.

target: orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978), base region; corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017) in sympetalous families
reason: The base of the lip, expressed as a region of an existing FLOPO class. Choose labellum or corolla lip from the family of the flora.
A comparative quality with a count ('3 longer ones'). The part is named elsewhere in the sentence.
French/English for a whorl or series ('in 3 circles'). Like 'whorl' in the previous review, a generic part that needs the organ it belongs to.
The (often sterile) anther borne by a staminode. Narrower than anther. 'Filiform' and 'bifid' in the examples may belong to the staminode itself, so check how they were assigned.
French 'slit'. Used both for pollen apertures and for anther dehiscence slits. Like 'slit' in the previous review, a generic part that needs its organ.
French 'line' (lines of lenticels, radiating lines). Like 'line' in the previous review, a generic word that needs its organ, and often a pattern rather than a part.
Glands of the disc in male flowers: an existing FLOPO class, part of a qualified whole.

target: portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656), whole flower (PO_0009046) + male (PATO_0000384) (pattern 12)
reason: Glands of male flowers (e.g. alternisepalous disc glands). 'gland' maps to PO_0005656 per the previous review, and the sex goes on the whole. If the flora says these are disc glands, use FLOPO_0986045.
French 'alvéole' means a pit of a receptacle, a cavity, or a locule, depending on context. Too ambiguous without the organ.
A shape quality ('à appendices cylindriques'). The part is the appendage.
